close_reason:
Added 'Concurrency' rustdoc section to SessionClient covering all four contract points from the bead:
- Send + Sync (callers can use from any tokio task)
- Clones share underlying reqwest::Client connection pool (clone freely, don't construct independent SessionClients)
- Concurrent calls are safe but UNORDERED — for inter-call ordering use JMAP batch + ResultReference
- Calls are cancel-safe at .await points; at-most-once delivery requires caller-side idempotency

Also added a const _: fn() = || { ... } compile-time assertion in the tests module locking SessionClient: Send + Sync. If JmapClient or Session loses Send/Sync upstream, this halts the build immediately instead of silently breaking the contract at consumer build time.

cargo build --tests, cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc all green. Committed as 1fdb359.
description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-client/src/methods/mod.rs:260-294 (`SessionClient` doc + definition).

`SessionClient` derives `Clone` and the rustdoc says (line 268-271):
```
/// `Clone` is derived because `JmapClient` is itself cheap-to-clone (it
/// already implements `Clone` and `with_chat_session` clones one
/// internally), enabling parallel-task fan-out with one bound session.
```

What the contract does NOT say:

1. **Send / Sync**: not declared explicitly. Both auto-derive (`JmapClient` is Send+Sync because it holds reqwest::Client through Arc, `Session` is Send+Sync because all fields are owned String/HashMap), but the contract is silent. A caller reading the doc to decide "can I move this into a `tokio::spawn`?" has to guess or read the impl. Workspace policy is verbose elsewhere about Debug-redaction and Clone semantics — Send/Sync deserves the same treatment.

2. **Concurrent-call semantics**: "parallel-task fan-out" implies concurrent calls are OK, but what they actually do is unstated:
   - Do two clones share a connection pool? (Yes — `JmapClient` wraps `reqwest::Client` which has an internal connection pool, so clones share.)
   - Do clones share session state? (Each clone has its own `Session` value, but the inner `JmapClient` is reference-counted to the same HTTP layer.)
   - Are concurrent `.call()` operations on the same `SessionClient` safe? (Yes, but never said.)
   - Is the order of concurrent requests preserved? (No — JMAP allows pipelining but reqwest doesn't guarantee response ordering across concurrent calls. Spec-relevant for ResultReference-bearing batches.)

3. **Cancel-safety at await points**: every public async method does an `await` on `call_internal`. If a caller wraps the call in a `tokio::select!` and drops it, is the underlying HTTP state coherent? (reqwest is cancel-safe; the contract should say so.)

Caller impact: a caller wanting to write a multi-tab chat UI with a worker-per-tab cannot tell from the contract whether one shared `JmapClient` cloned per worker is safe (it is), or whether they should construct independent ones (they shouldn't — that defeats connection pooling). They'll guess wrong half the time.

Fix: add three sentences to the `SessionClient` doc:
- "`SessionClient` is `Send + Sync` and may be used from any task."
- "Cloning is cheap; the underlying `JmapClient` is reference-counted and clones share the HTTP connection pool."
- "Concurrent calls on a single `SessionClient` (or on clones) are safe but unordered; for ordered multi-method calls use a single JMAP request with `ResultReference`s."
title: SessionClient concurrency contract undocumented (Clone, parallel-task fan-out)
